messages.subject: Lincomb for random slope model
parts:
I'm sorry if this is  s dumb question, but I'm not sure
that I'm setting up a lincomb correctly. The model is
a random slope model:

inla(Reaction ~ 1 + Days + f(Subject,Days,model="iid"), . . .)

where Subject is a factor, identifying individuals in groups of
10 observations 308, 308, ... , 308, 319, 319, ...
and Days is numeric, as rep(0:9,times=18). So we have 18 Subjects
with 10 contigous observations on each, and we're estimating 18
random effects.

I want to compute the full random slope for each Subject.
I've tried many formulations of inla.make.lincomb
and as a check, I would expect that the mean of the first reported
lincomb to be zero since the first value of Days is zero;
but it isn't. (Is this expectation correct?)

Obviously I'm misunderstanding something here.
Can anyone tell me what I'm doing wrong (and if possible
provide a bit more explanation of how the lincomb should be set up)?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Lincomb for random slope model
parts:
as a side-note, I would mention the model 'intslope' that combine this
intercept-slope model into one f(), for which what you want is directly
there, as far as I see.
